steps.text: Courier has a thick stack of paper in his hands as he stands by the shredder. The first page says 'Kjerag Logistics System Proposal'.
He wears a heavy, hesitant expression on his face, but eventually extends the proposal toward the shredder.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Wait.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Mr. Bison...

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Why are you destroying the proposal?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Because it failed.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: I'm your logistics lecturer. You're not the one who decides what's failed.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Besides, you didn't have that look on your face when you first told me you were drafting a proposal for Kjerag's logistics system.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: May I have a look?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Yes, sir.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Pretty comprehensive.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: You've covered all the bases, from manpower to cost to transportation method to storage.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: It's a solid proposal.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: There's only one problem left to solve—the engineering issues in Terra Nullius.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: A Terra Nullius exists between the zone of actual Kjerag control and our neighboring countries.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: A full-fledged logistics system requires a more developed transportation infrastructure, but neighboring countries will not simply sit and watch as Kjerag develops Terra Nullius.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I could not find a way to solve this problem, so I decided to give up.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: If I recall correctly, I've discussed solutions to similar issues.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: One way is to invest in an international logistics company.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: In that case, there's no need to write a proposal at all—just leave it to a developed international logistics firm, like MountainDash Logistics.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: We discussed this too.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: In order to effectively operate in Kjerag, MountainDash would need someone reliable to manage local operations—someone like you.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: But you refused. Do you regret that choice?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Well—no.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Another way is to leave Kjerag and establish my own logistics firm.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: As clear as such a firm's Kjerag links would be, it would face a lot less opposition, as long as it does not belong to Kjerag officially.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I'm clear on that much, but—

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: You're not willing to accept it.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Just like you turned down my offer.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Because either way means leaving Karlan Trade, perhaps even leaving Kjerag.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: It's the thought of leaving Kjerag that you really want to banish, isn't it?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I realized that everything in this proposal was written with the assumption that I would manage it personally.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: The proposal was custom-made for myself. Implementing it means I'm the one who would need to leave Kjerag.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I was too arrogant.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: So you're just giving up on the proposal?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I'll write a new one for the Master, so that he may find the right man.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: So you're just giving up on the opportunity?

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: I know how much Kjerag means to you.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: But this is a chance for you to show your value, isn't it?

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: If you're not interested—

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Why did you choose to study at Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Thank you for the kind words, but my mind is made up.
Courier snatches the proposal from Bison before he can react.
Before he can put the proposal in the shredder, however, he hears a crowing from behind him.
The fowlbeast is even faster than he, and whisks the proposal away in its beak. He is familiar with this fowlbeast—Tenzin.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: ...Master.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Your thoughts seem have been heading down a dangerous path lately.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I... I'm sorry, Master.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: But—

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: But I'm also curious. Let's have you implement the proposal, Weiss.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Mapping, route planning, negotiating with the villages, deploying personnel...

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Once you actually put things in place, you may find that they don't require your presence as much as you assumed they would.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Yes, Master.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Wait.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: I'll go with you.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: But—

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: You have an avalanche warning team, don't you?

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Just treat me as one of them.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Let me see up close whether you really can do what you think you can.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Yes, Master.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Are you sure about this, Mr. SilverAsh?

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: I am.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: It's high time Weiss took a good look at himself.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: *Huff*... *huff*...

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Here, take my hand, Master.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: No need. What of the others?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: They're already at the summit.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: This trail may be a little difficult for you, sir.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: You're just trying to get rid of me, aren't you, Weiss?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Of course not.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: But one who spends his time in an office doing paperwork is bound to be less active than those of us who spend most of our time outdoors, no?

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Heh.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: We can take a break here.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: The team at the summit can wait a while. They'll understand.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Let's go.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: We can't delay the surveying on my account.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: As you wish.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: You're right, it has been a long time since I last climbed a hill.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: You used to be very good at it.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: I took after my mother.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Not so much these days.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: You are still very much like her. You've just learned to hide it better.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: By the way, I never told you this, but the day I took you in, I was only out there because my sisters made me go hunting with them.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I knew.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Did you?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Your sisters are not as tight-lipped as you are.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: By chance, they had you join them on a hunting trip in the mountains that day. By chance, you got separated from them. By chance, you ran into me.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: It was snowing heavily that day. You were lost too, weren't you?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: You put on a brave face, told me to come with you, and took me to the Silverash manor.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: When my grandparents came and begged the old master to take me on as a servant after I had lost my parents at a young age, it was you who persuaded him, saying that you wanted a male companion around your own age.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: And so, I became part of Clan Silverash.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Perhaps...

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Are your grandparents well?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Thanks to you, my grandfather is quite the man in Turicum's senior center, and my grandmother has opened a little shop of her own. They're rather enjoying their lives.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: To me, Matterhorn is a guardian, one who has always served my family. I almost take him for granted. You're different.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: You, I took under my own wing—at least, that's what I thought at the time.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Besides, you were quick and nimble. For a while, I had you carry my messages to others, and their messages back to me.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: In truth, I was just trying to show you off.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: There's no need to feel guilty about it.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: It gave my life meaning.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: After all, I was a wild child who popped suddenly into the family. My presence was unwelcome to many.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: How can you be sure I did not use your name for my own designs in the process?

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: If you did, you hid it well.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Heh. How very you.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Besides—

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: At first, I did not enjoy running around the hills and mountains.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: With time, however, as I walked the forests and the mountain trails—

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: As I climbed the snowy peaks—

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: As I breathed the air atop the peaks, and watched the spectacle of the mountains in the distance against the blue sky—

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I felt happy.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I began to enjoy it.

steps.name: Kjerag Warrior
steps.text: Captain, Mast—SilverAsh. You're here.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Report.

steps.name: Kjerag Warrior
steps.text: We have good news and bad news.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Start with the good news.

steps.name: Kjerag Warrior
steps.text: This is the last location we're scheduled to visit on this survey trip. We've successfully plotted the Terra Nullius between Kjerag and our neighboring countries.

steps.name: Kjerag Warrior
steps.text: We have also located all the independent villages in Terra Nullius.

steps.name: Kjerag Warrior
steps.text: The experts have already plotted the most efficient and cost-effective route for transportation, assuming that the villages could be persuaded to act as hubs and depots.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: And the bad news?

steps.name: Scholar
steps.text: The bad news is... although plans for the route are essentially in place, and costs as well as time required are largely within acceptable boundaries...

steps.name: Scholar
steps.text: Not all villages have accepted our proposal.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: That's also to be expected. Which ones are they?

steps.name: Scholar
steps.text: Take a look.

steps.name: Scholar
steps.text: These few villages, especially this one.

steps.name: Scholar
steps.text: They are not friendly to outsiders. The village headman, at least, seems reasonable, but opposition from the others puts him in an awkward position.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Wait, this village...

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Pack it up.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Abandoning the plan?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I'm going back to Turicum.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: The key to persuading those villagers lies there.

steps.name: Station Staff
steps.text: Just to make sure I understand this correctly, Mr. Weiss... you need to persuade the villagers in order to establish a logistics route.

steps.name: Station Staff
steps.text: That's why you want me to write a letter to my father.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: The villagers hold your father in high-esteem, after all.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Of course, we're not going to force you, if you're not willing.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I've already told you the potential risks, and the benefits.

steps.name: Station Staff
steps.text: Of course I'm willing!

steps.name: Station Staff
steps.text: If not for your recommendation, I would never have come to Kjerag, and I wouldn't have found this job.

steps.name: Station Staff
steps.text: Besides, it would be a dream come true if you really managed to establish such a route around Kjerag!

steps.name: Station Staff
steps.text: I'll get to it at once!

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Wait.

steps.name: Station Staff
steps.text: Yes?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: It's been a while since you've been home, hasn't it? If there's anything you want to send back to your family, I'll deliver it for you.

steps.name: Station Staff
steps.text: I-I couldn't trouble you with that.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: It's no trouble. These villages on the frontier rarely get supplies from Kjerag.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Besides, it would improve the chances of swaying your father.

steps.name: Station Staff
steps.text: If you put it that way, I guess it would be rude to refuse.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: You know the staff at Turicum Station well.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: It's the main hub for all mail and cargo that goes through Kjerag.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I like it.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Is that why you chose to study logistics at Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I enjoy running through the mountains.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I enjoy seeing the expressions on faces when messages, letters, and packages are delivered.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Be it your face, or any others.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Be it expressions of joy, pain, or sorrow.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Maybe it all began with a childhood whim of yours—

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: But I began to enjoy the feeling.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: The feeling of linking people together.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Besides...

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: At first, I didn't understand why you wouldn't give me and Matterhorn specific duties at Karlan Trade.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: With time, however, I began to understand—

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: You wanted us to decide our own futures.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: I never thought of myself as your master.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: That's why I never thought about determining your fates for you.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: But you never tell people what you think.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: On this trip, I kept pondering why you wanted to tag along.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: It didn't seem like something worth your time and effort, whether you meant to urge me to stay, or urge me to go.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Now, I'm beginning to understand.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Tell me more.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Now is not the time, not yet.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Perhaps you've forgotten—

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: But we've been to this village that we're about to visit before, more than a decade ago.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Yes?

steps.name: Station Staff
steps.text: Here's the letter, Mr. Weiss!

steps.name: Station Staff
steps.text: And this is the stuff to send to my folks.

steps.name: Station Staff
steps.text: It might be a little too much. If you don't think it works—

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: It's fine. Give them to this man here.

steps.name: Station Staff
steps.text: Wait, isn't that Sir Enciodes—

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: No, he's a member of the Kjerag Expedition, of which I am the captain.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: ...I see. I remember it now.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: I'll take it.

steps.name: Station Staff
steps.text: H-Here you go, sir.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Ugh... it's heavy.

steps.name: Old Villager
steps.text: Who are you?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Have you forgotten me, Sage Edwards?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I am Weiss, captain of the Kjerag Expedition. This one here is Matterhorn, a warrior under my charge.

steps.name: Old Villager
steps.text: Ah, yes, I remember you.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Come and greet the sage, Matterhorn.

steps.name: Matterhorn?
steps.text: It's been a while, sir.

steps.name: Old Villager
steps.text: Very good, very good.

steps.name: Old Villager
steps.text: At first I thought you were hillmen coming from who-knows-where. Little could I imagine that you were heralds of Kjerag.

steps.name: Old Villager
steps.text: How is that son of mine, Chris, doing in Kjerag?

steps.name: Matterhorn?
steps.text: We came to deliver Chris's letter, sir.

steps.name: Matterhorn?
steps.text: Along with the gifts he prepared for his family.

steps.name: Old Villager
steps.text: So many things? My goodness. He shouldn't have.

steps.name: Matterhorn?
steps.text: (Softly) Whew—

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: (Whisper) Good work, Master.

steps.name: Matterhorn?
steps.text: (Whisper) Thanks.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Chris is doing very well in Kjerag. He is in line for a promotion to manager soon.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Please, go ahead and read the letter. It also explains why we're here.

steps.name: Old Villager
steps.text: I see. I know what you're here for.

steps.name: Old Villager
steps.text: Let's go inside.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: May we count on you to convince the villagers, then?

steps.name: Old Villager
steps.text: It's no small business. There will be a lot to discuss.

steps.name: Old Villager
steps.text: But don't worry. With Chris's letter and your guarantee, I'm sure they'll come around.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Please feel free to let me know if our presence is warranted.

steps.name: Old Villager
steps.text: Very good, very good.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Do you remember now, Master?

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Hard not to, after carrying so much all this way.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I wanted you to feel for yourself the importance of logistics.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Besides, I helped you carry half of it.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: That day, I wanted to see what the outside was like, after my lessons.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: So I hopped on one of the downhill transport carts, and dragged you along with me.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I was scared out of my wits.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: It was actually Matterhorn whom I wanted to bring first.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: But thinking again, I was sure he would try to stop me, so I turned to you.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: What made you so sure I wouldn't try to stop you?

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: You never stopped anyone from doing anything stupid, even me.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Besides, you wanted to see the outside too, didn't you?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I told you to turn back when we descended the mountain and saw nothing but a barren plain.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: You just wouldn't listen.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: We were getting chewed out by Mother regardless. We might as well take a few more steps forward. Maybe there would be a surprise lying in wait for us.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: We would've starved to death if I didn't steal some food from the kitchen before we left.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I was cursing you under my breath all the way.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: I thought you were grateful to me for saving your life.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: No one wants to starve in the wilderness.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Sure enough. I certainly don't.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: That's why I began to regret it when we ran out of food.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Fortunately, we found this village. Old Edwards was sweeping snow from his door. His hair wasn't white yet.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Do you remember how he almost chased us away because he thought we were hillmen?

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: I do.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: You whipped up the name of some expedition out of nowhere and said you were the captain.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Somehow, he believed you, invited us into his home, and treated us to warm cystymilk.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: What were you thinking at the time?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: The old master had told me that there were people with ill-intent towards Clan Silverash. I thought it inadvisable to say the name of the family.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: It's always the leader who has the target on his back, which was why I said I was the captain.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I thought it was a genius idea at the time. Now it seems so childish.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: It's alright. I thought it was a genius idea at the time too.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Otherwise, I wouldn't have claimed to be the bravest warrior under your banner.
Courier falls silent for some reason.
He turns to look in the direction of Kjerag.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: When we got back, Madam punished us by making us eat outside.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: That was the harshest punishment Mother ever gave me.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: I still remember the tears in her eyes—

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: 'If you want to be out in the ice and snow so much, you might as well eat in it!'

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: That was it.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: It was Lady Enya who delivered our meals the first day, then Lady Ensia the second day.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: On day three, the old master came out to eat with us together.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: In the end, Madam let us back in.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Mother always treated you as her son, and I treated you as my brother.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: And I know why you've come along.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: You wanted to tell me that you'll never forget the ties that bind me and the Silverashes.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: And you wanted to hear the answer from my heart, directly.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: What's your answer?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: My answer is—

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: That proposal was not the product of my arrogance.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: It's something that only I can do.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Therefore...

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I request a leave of absence from Kjerag, Master.
The company registration office is just ahead.
Courier clutches the documents in his hand tightly and gulps.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: You look just like I did when I was brooding over whether to knock on the door of House Caster.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Were you afraid, at the time?

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Afraid? I was excited, excited for the surprises that might lie behind the door.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I've done many bold things, and I believe there are many ways in which I can serve you.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: But leaving Kjerag was the one thing that I never thought I would do.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I used to believe it was out of loyalty.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: People say I'm lucky to have loyal lieutenants like Weiss and Matterhorn.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: They don't realize I have no interest in blind loyalty, and it's not your loyalty that makes me trust you.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: We happen to be of similar minds, and I happen to not have strayed from the path yet. That's all there is to it, isn't it?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Perhaps.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: The Weiss I know isn't just a kind and gentle soul.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: He watches everything and keeps it to himself. People believe he doesn't think for himself. Little do they know that he has long found the answer.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Do you know my answer?

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: All I know that we're still of similar minds on the matter.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: You and I both know that I'm the only man for the job.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I just wasn't sure if I'm ready to take this step.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: You went to all the effort, coming on this trip with me, just to tell me—

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: You know, and you remember.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: You came to see me off, didn't you?

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: I was waiting for the most nimble Itra in the mountains to muster the courage to descend into the vast unknown.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: You will lose your most loyal lieutenant.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: I will gain a new friend, an interesting ally, a worthy competitor.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Master. I expect this is the last time I'll call you that. I'll leave your side and leave Clan Silverash.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I'll establish my own logistics company.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: It will not be registered in Kjerag. It will focus on the development of routes in the Terra Nullius surrounding Kjerag, in conjunction with MountainDash Logistics.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Its operations will not be limited to logistics. It will participate in the development of villages in Terra Nullius, and improve the state of transportation around Kjerag.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Perhaps it will even build a new nomadic city on the outskirts of Kjerag.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: Will it be Karlan Trade's ally, or enemy?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I can only promise that it will remain a friend to Kjerag. It was you who taught me that there is no such thing as an absolute ally or enemy in the realm of business.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: You think you can persuade Bison to work with you?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: Between a worthwhile partner and a subordinate whose loyalty is uncertain, he knows which choice to make.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: My name won't carry much weight outside Kjerag.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: The things I've learned over the years by your side and from Rhodes Island will last me a while.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: I'm never going to hear the end of it from Ensia about how I keep driving people away.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: You'll deserve it. Of course, Silverash Manor is still my home, and I could hardly be faulted for coming home once in a while.

steps.name: SilverAsh
steps.text: What should we call this company, this new friend of Kjerag?

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: I think 'Courier Logistics' will do nicely.
